# Crumb & Copper: Weekend Sourdough Subscription Launch

## 1. Instagram plan

### Format: a 20-second Reel, followed by a carousel

**Why a Reel.** We have two goals: sign-ups, and as many locals as possible hearing about the launch.

- **Reach:** The last Reel reached 6,400 people. That is about twice our follower count, so it got in front of non-followers. The carousel reached 2,700 and the single photo 1,900.
- **Clicks:** The Reel's link clicks (38) were nearly level with the carousel's (41). The single photo got only 12.

**Why a carousel afterwards.** The carousel converts better per viewer: 1.5% of people reached clicked, against 0.6% for the Reel. It also gets the most saves (95), which suits "I'll sign up on payday." Post a 4-slide follow-up carousel 3–4 days after the Reel and pin both to the profile.

**Caveat:** Each format has only one example post, so treat this as a direction rather than proof. Check link clicks and sign-ups after 7 days.

### Reel scene list (vertical 9:16, on-screen text for viewers watching with sound off)

| Time | Scene | On-screen text |
|---|---|---|
| 0–2 s | Dark kitchen, light switch flicks on, clock shows 5:00 | "5am, Saturday." |
| 2–6 s | Close-up of hands shaping and folding dough | "Shaped by hand, every week" |
| 6–9 s | Scoring a loaf, loading the oven | "Certified organic flour" |
| 9–12 s | Loaves out of the oven, crust crackle audible | "One of these could be yours" |
| 12–15 s | A regular collects a bagged loaf at the counter and smiles | "Pick up 8–11am Saturdays" |
| 15–18 s | Copper card on cream background | "4 loaves a month · $36 · save $4" |
| 18–20 s | Tote bag on the counter beside a loaf | "First 50 sign-ups get a free tote · Link in bio" |

- **Audio:** Use real kitchen sound with a soft acoustic track underneath.
- **Cover frame:** The loaves-out shot with "Sourdough subscription" in serif.

**Follow-up carousel slides:**
1. How it works
2. Price and saving
3. Pick-up times
4. Buckwheat & rice loaf, with the full allergen note

### Caption (111 words)

> Our 5am shift just got some regulars. 🍞
>
> From 2 May, you can subscribe to our sourdough: one loaf every Saturday, four a month, for $36. That's $4 less than buying at the counter.
>
> Collect yours between 8 and 11am at the shop.
>
> Every loaf is made with certified organic flour. There's also a buckwheat & rice loaf made with no gluten ingredients. It's baked alongside our wheat bread, so it isn't suitable for coeliacs.
>
> The first 50 people to sign up get a free Crumb & Copper tote.
>
> Sign up via the link in our bio 👉 crumbandcopper.example.com/subscribe
>
> Tag someone who'd fight you for the heel.

### Hashtags (8)

`#sourdough` `#sourdoughsubscription` `#localbakery` `#shoplocal` `#realbread` `#organicflour` `#[suburb]eats` `#crumbandcopper`

Replace `[suburb]` with our suburb tag. It is the hashtag most likely to reach locals.

---

## 2. A5 flyer

### Copy

- **Top band:** CRUMB & COPPER · Neighbourhood bakery
- **Headline:** Your Saturday loaf, sorted.
- **Subhead:** Weekend sourdough subscription · from 2 May
- **Price:** $36/month
- **Price line:** 4 loaves a month, one every Saturday. Save $4 on counter prices.
- **Details:**
  - Pick up 8–11am Saturdays at the shop, [shop address]
  - Made with certified organic flour
  - Buckwheat & rice loaf option* (no gluten ingredients)
- **Badge:** FREE TOTE for the first 50 sign-ups
- **Call to action:** Sign up today. Scan the code or visit crumbandcopper.example.com/subscribe
- **Footer (allergens):** \*Our buckwheat & rice loaf contains no gluten ingredients but is baked in the same kitchen and ovens as our wheat bread. It is not suitable for coeliacs or anyone with a gluten allergy. Our kitchen handles wheat, sesame, milk, eggs and tree nuts.

### Layout by zone (A5, 148 × 210 mm)

| Zone | Height | Content |
|---|---|---|
| A: Top band | ~8% | Charcoal band with the wordmark in cream |
| B: Hero photo | ~34% | Saturday loaves on our own counter. The tote badge overlaps the bottom-right corner |
| C: Headline | ~12% | Serif headline and sans subhead, left-aligned |
| D: Price | ~10% | Large copper "$36/month" and the price line |
| E: Details | ~13% | Three rows, each with a copper bullet |
| F: Call to action | ~13% | QR code (at least 22 mm) on the left, call to action and full URL on the right |
| G: Footer | ~8% | Allergen note, separated by a thin copper rule |

### Visual direction

**Photography**
- Use real staff, real loaves and the real counter.
- Light with morning window light: warm, slightly underexposed, visible flour dust and crust texture.
- No stock images and no styled props we don't use.

**Colour**
- Cream `#F5EBDD` as the background.
- Charcoal `#2B2B2B` for all body text.
- Copper `#B87333` for the price, rules, bullets and the badge ring only.

**Typography**
- Headlines in a warm serif, such as Georgia or a similar bookish serif.
- Body text in a clean sans-serif at 10–11 pt minimum. Footer at 8 pt minimum.
- Sentence case throughout, which reads as friendlier and less corporate.

**Accessibility (contrast checked against WCAG)**

| Combination | Contrast | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Charcoal on cream | ≈12:1 | Passes for all text sizes |
| Copper on cream | ≈3.2:1 | Large text only (≥18 pt, or ≥14 pt bold) |

- Never set small copper text.
- Badge text is cream on charcoal.
- Print the URL in full next to the QR code, for people who don't scan.
- Meaning never relies on colour alone.
- Use uncoated matte stock to avoid glare under café lights.

## 3. Note to Mary

Hi Mary, I changed a few lines so everything we print is accurate:

- **"25% off" → "save $4 a month."** Four $10 loaves cost $40, so $36 is 10% off.
- **"100% organic" → "made with certified organic flour."** The seed mix isn't certified.
- **"Gluten-free" → "buckwheat & rice loaf, no gluten ingredients,"** plus a coeliac warning and our allergen list. It shares ovens with wheat and isn't tested, so a gluten-free claim could make someone ill and break labelling rules.

Could you confirm three things?

1. What do subscribers get in five-Saturday months?
2. What is the shop address for the flyer?
3. Is 2 May the first pick-up?

Everything else is as you wrote it.
